reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Sunday 2 August
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Monday 27 July to Saturday 1 August.
reports.summary: The week from Monday 27 July to Saturday 1 August averaged about 22.8 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 41.9% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Tuesday 28 July, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 49.3% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Wednesday 29 July and lowest on Monday 27 July.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Tuesday 28 July, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 49.3% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 7.4 GW average output on Tuesday 28 July.
Solar was strongest on Friday 31 July, averaging about 4.6 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 7.0 GW across the period, rising highest on Wednesday 29 July and falling lowest on Monday 27 July.
Measured generation was highest on Wednesday 29 July, at roughly 24.7 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Tuesday 28 July
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Tuesday 28 July had the strongest renewable share at 49.3%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Monday 27 July
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 4.4 GW on Monday 27 July. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Wednesday 29 July
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 9.5 GW on Wednesday 29 July. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 49.3% on Tuesday 28 July
• Highest average wind output: ~7.4 GW on Tuesday 28 July
• Highest average solar output: ~4.6 GW on Friday 31 July
• Highest average gas output: ~9.5 GW on Wednesday 29 July

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-08-02/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
